topic: A person discovers their child has the same teacher they had
text: When Old Man Grimbly told me his boy was takin' his lessons from Master Alden, the same as I did when the rains were scarce and the crops were thin, it caught me like a harvest breeze. Master Alden, a man of the books and the faith, as wise as the roots run deep. It feels like the old times are still in the turn of the soil, even as the seasons change. I remember the shock of the cold on my face as I walked to the school, the sound of his voice cuttin' through the quiet of the mornin'. I can see young Grimbly now, his eyes wide as the full moon, sittin' where I once did, learnin' the ways of the world. It’s the circle, I suppose, the same as the plow turns the earth, year after year.
